# Area audit: going online

Step 2.110. Area 7 of [LEADS.md](../LEADS.md): "The founder and the leagues that will depend on it. It runs for real: a real database, a worker, releases that can be taken back, backups that have been restored once, alarms, no secret where it should not be, and a written way to handle each kind of failure."

Written 2026-11-17 by the area lead for going online, from build branch commit `7443bb1`. It changes no code, no test and no plan. Line numbers given for files are as of that commit. It starts from [STAGE-1-REPORT.md](../STAGE-1-REPORT.md), the first audit of this area, and goes further.

## 1. In plain words

**Can the first online test copy be put up safely today? No.** Today the website refuses, on purpose, to start anywhere but on a computer: it says so in one sentence and stops (section 6.1, case 18). That refusal goes away with the last part of step 2.93, which is on the Test 2 line. But even once every step on that line has landed, four things would still stop the supervised session or leave the copy unsafe, and none of them is in any plan:

1. **The website and the worker cannot check the test database's certificate** (finding H1). Supabase's database certificate comes from Supabase's own authority, not one a computer trusts by default (the lead saw this on 2026-11-13). The website has no setting to be given that authority's file, so on the test copy it will stop with "the database could not be reached". Shown here on a real PostgreSQL whose certificate comes from a made-up authority.
2. **Nobody can read the test copy's sign-in codes** (finding H2). The page that shows kept emails on a computer is refused on the test copy by design, and the replacement chosen in record 075 (codes kept in the test database and read by a script at the founder's terminal) is in no step. Without it, the league's owner cannot finish signing up, and the walk stops at its first screen.
3. **Step 2.95 must settle four things before the session** (findings M20 and M11): that a push to the build branch does not restart the test copy in the middle of a game, where the database changes are applied on Render's free instance, that the image carries the file that tells the website which database is the tracker's (`supabase/site.json`; without it the website refuses to start), and how the database logins are made.
4. **Nothing on the test copy says it is made up** (finding M4). On a computer every league page says "A made-up league on this computer"; on the test copy, a stranger or a tester would see what looks like a real league, with nothing to stop real children's names being typed in.

The founder's own part before the session is three things: a new password for the test database (the first was pasted into a chat), Supabase's certificate file, and a Render account. The worker is not needed for the walk and cannot start on any hosted database yet (finding H3), so its paid instance (about $7 a month) can wait.

**After those, the session can be held safely, with made-up data only. The product would still not be ready for real people:** nobody is told when anything breaks (H4: no error reports, no outside checks, no alerts), no backup has ever been restored and no step will restore one (H5), and the worker can never start on a hosted database until step 2.112's planned change is corrected (H3, shown here to fail exactly as written).

**What held up, tried on a real PostgreSQL here:** all twenty database changes apply in order on an empty database in under half a second, and on top of a database that stands where the test copy stands (nine changes); on the in-process PostgreSQL the tests use, the newest change applied on top of a database already holding two made-up leagues changed no row of any other table; a change that fails half-way leaves nothing behind; every setting that is missing or wrong stops the website and the worker with a sentence that names the setting and never its value (28 cases); the guard that keeps the platform away from the Al-Hadi tracker's database refused every address that tried to reach it; the worker started on a real PostgreSQL for the first time, survived its database going away for 80 seconds, said so on its health address after a minute, and was back within five seconds of the database's return; a dump and restore of a database holding two made-up leagues brought back every row, every rule of the league fence and every grant; and the website built with made-up secrets in its settings carries none of them in anything the build produced.

| Findings | High | Medium | Low |
| -------- | ---- | ------ | --- |
| Count    | 5    | 20     | 9   |

## 2. How this was done, and what was not checked

- **Read:** the spec's T1, T8 (where T1 and T9 point for operations), T9 and T10 with their exit tests; decision T-270; [STAGE-1-REPORT.md](../STAGE-1-REPORT.md); the plan's lines for steps 2.92 to 2.100, 2.112, 2.115, 2.140 and 2.193 and this step's own line; the rows the 2.105 audit handed over (its lines 634, 756, 800, 841, 856 and findings M14 and M15); every file in `docs/operations/`; records 018, 052, 053, 055, 075 and 079; the web app's and the worker's start-up, settings and health code; the database connection code, the migration runner, the queue and the queue's schema check; the sign-in adapter's session check; the tracker's own database connection (`packages/database/src/live-stats/postgres.ts`); `.github/workflows/`.
- **Run, on this computer, with made-up values only.** This machine has PostgreSQL 16 installed (`/usr/lib/postgresql/16/bin`). A database server of its own was started inside the repository's git-ignored `.local/pg`, listening on this computer only, with encryption on and a certificate signed by a made-up authority made here, as Supabase's is signed by Supabase's own. The tables' owner was made the way Supabase's `postgres` user is (not a superuser; may create roles; bypasses the fence), so what works only for a superuser would show. On it:
  - the repository's own migration runner (`connectPostgresDriver` and `applyMigrations`), from scratch scripts outside the repository;
  - the built website (`node scripts/web.mjs start`) and the worker (`apps/worker/src/main.ts`), each started with nothing but the settings named for that case (`env -i`), in staging and production modes: 22 cases for the website, 6 for the worker;
  - a stand-in for the sign-in service's one start-up question (`GET /auth/v1/settings`), answering on this computer only;
  - the database stopped and started under a running worker;
  - `pg_dump` and `pg_restore` as the tables' owner;
  - the tracker's database connection with addresses that try to switch encryption off;
  - `npm audit` on both lockfiles; a search of the whole git history for the shapes of real keys; a build of the website with made-up secrets in its settings, then a search of everything it produced.
- **Also run:** `npm run check`, and the tests of the local-only pages, the website's and the worker's start-up and the queue's schema check (4 files, 47 tests, all passed).
- **Not checked, because it needs a real service, an account or the founder:** Supabase itself (its PostgreSQL 17, its pooler, its sign-in service, its backups and its limits); Render (its free and paid instances, its logs, its deploys and roll-backs, how many proxies stand in front of a request); anything over the internet; any price. Where this audit says how a vendor behaves, it says so as the vendor describes itself as far as known on this day, and the session or the sign-up confirms it.
- **Not checked, because it cannot run yet:** the website serving pages in staging or production (it refuses to start there until step 2.93's last part), so nothing was asked of it over the network: not its "do not index" answer, not its error pages, not the local-only pages' "not found" answer. The two-league test was not run on the real PostgreSQL: its harness takes the in-process database (PGlite) only, and changing a test is not this audit's to do.
- **Cleaned up:** the database server, its files and the scratch copies are in `.local` (git-ignored) and the scratchpad; nothing else on this computer was changed.

### 3.3 What would stop the session, or leave the copy unsafe

In the order the session would meet them:

1. **H1:** at step 8 the website cannot check the database's certificate and stops.
2. **M20:** at step 8, if Render deploys every push of the build branch, a landing by the build restarts the copy during the walk; where the database changes run on the free instance is not settled; an image without `supabase/site.json` refuses to start.
3. **H2:** at step 12 the owner cannot read their code, and the walk stops.
4. **M4:** from step 8 on, the copy looks like a real league to anyone who opens it, and nothing stops real people's details being typed into it.
5. **M5:** at step 9, forty checks by hand in one session, each a chance to misread a result.

The first four are the proposed steps marked "(TEST 2)" in section 11. The fifth does not make the session unsafe, only slower and easier to get wrong, so its step is proposed without the mark.

## 4. What is finished, and what is not

**Finished and tried here on a real PostgreSQL:**

- Every setting is checked once at start, by the website and the worker, and every refusal names the setting in one sentence without its value (6.1).
- The guard that keeps the platform off the Al-Hadi tracker's database, in both programs (6.1, cases 6 to 9).
- The migration runner: in order, with no gap, once each, a failed file rolled back whole, a database ahead of the folder accepted and left alone (6.2).
- The league fence's roles: the app's login is refused at start if it is a superuser, bypasses the fence or owns the tables (6.1, cases 13 and 14); with no league set it sees no league (6.2).
- The worker: starts with pg-boss on PostgreSQL, keeps going while its database is away, says so on its health address, and recovers by itself (6.5).
- The email-confirmation check of step 2.115, against a stand-in of the sign-in service: on, off and unreachable (6.1, cases 17 to 19).
- Secrets kept out of what the website builds and out of every start-up message (6.3).

**Built, but tried only on the in-process database or on a computer:** every area of the website on the database (step 2.93's landed parts), the sign-in adapter for Supabase (against recorded answers), the league-making and league-removing tools, the bin, the job queue's handover to pg-boss (now also started here on PostgreSQL 16).

**Planned and not built:** the website serving in staging (2.93's last part), the image, the release command and going back (2.95), the queue's own schema (2.112), nothing unfinished in production (2.140), the automatic security checks (2.99), the browser's safety rules before real accounts (2.98).

**In no plan:** the certificate setting (H1), reading the test copy's codes (H2), error reports, outside checks and alerts (H4), a restore and its rehearsal (H5), four of the eight written procedures (M6), the made-up notice on the test copy (M4), the database logins for a new copy (M11), measuring any speed or size figure (M14), and the preview copy of each change (M17).

## 5. Findings

Severity as in [LEADS.md](../LEADS.md): **High**, the product cannot go online, or would go online unsafe, or a failure would lose a league's data or leave nobody knowing; **Medium**, must be fixed before real people use it; **Low**, tidying. "(TEST 2)" marks what the supervised session cannot be held safely without.

### High

**H1 (TEST 2). The website and the worker cannot check the test database's certificate, and have no setting for it.** Both open their database through `createDatabase` (`packages/database/src/db/create-database.ts:51-52`), which takes the encryption setting from code, never from the address, and checks the server's certificate against the computer's own list of authorities (`sslSetting`, `packages/database/src/migrations/postgres-driver.ts:40-44`: `{ rejectUnauthorized: true }` with no `ca`). Neither program has a setting that could give it another authority's file (`apps/web/src/server/config-schema.ts`, `apps/worker/src/config-schema.ts`: no such field), and the address may not carry one (the guard refuses `sslrootcert` and every other such key, case 6). Supabase's database certificate is signed by Supabase's own authority: the lead found it on 2026-11-13 ("`ssl: 'verify'` needs their certificate passed as `ca` (this run used 'no-verify')", `STATUS.md` line 400). Only the league-making tool has a setting for it (`MIGRATION_DATABASE_CA`). _Proof:_ on PostgreSQL 16 here, with a certificate from a made-up authority, the right login and everything else right: "The web app cannot start: the database could not be reached to check its login role." (case 11) and the worker's "The worker cannot start: the database could not be reached to check its login role and queue schema." (case W4). With Node's own `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` pointed at that authority's file, both went past it (cases 12 and W6). _Spec:_ T4 §9, line 110 ("The production database accepts connections only from our servers, encrypted"), which means nothing unless the server is checked; the runner's own rule, "SSL is verified by default" (`apply-migrations.md`); T-30. Nothing in a plan, a record or a procedure names it. _What would happen without a fix:_ either the session stops at the website's first start, or someone reaches for `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` or for switching the check off under time pressure. Proposed step P1.

**H2 (TEST 2). Nobody can read the test copy's sign-in codes, so the league's owner cannot finish signing up.** With the real sign-in service, the codes are made by Supabase without sending anything and handed to our own email sender (record 018, "Codes"), which outside production keeps every email instead of sending it (T-140). On a computer, step 2.96's page shows them. On the test copy that page answers "not found" by construction (record 075, three gates), and record 075 chose another way for the test copy: "Option 5 [kept in the test copy's own database and read by a script at the founder's terminal], built when the test copy first sends an email … nothing is built for it now" (record 075, "Choice"). No step builds it: not 2.93's last part (which wires real sign-in), not 2.95, not 2.96. T-270 says the opposite of the record: "on the test copy every email is captured and read through the page of step 2.96" (`T1-stack-and-architecture.md` line 82), and the first-test line counts 2.96 as what lets "an owner made by the league-making tool … create an account" (`STATUS.md`, the first-test line). The worker's own capture in staging writes files to `EMAIL_CAPTURE_DIR` on the host's disk, which record 075 refused for the test copy (lost on every deploy, no shell to read it). _Proof:_ record 075; `grep` of `docs/build/STAGE-2.md` finds no step naming the table, the store or `read-kept-emails`. _Spec:_ T-140, T-201, T4 §10 (no code in a log). Proposed step P2. A fallback that needs no building (record 075's option 4: the lead gives the made-up owner a password in Supabase's dashboard) would let the founder sign in, but it tests a second way of making accounts, never the one real people will use; it should be written down only as the way out if P2 is late.

**H3. Step 2.112's database change cannot run on Supabase as written, so the worker can never start on a hosted database.** The step says: "`create schema if not exists pgboss authorization queue_owner`". On PostgreSQL 16 and later, only a role that may act as `queue_owner` can make it the owner of a schema; a role that merely created `queue_owner` may not, unless it is a superuser. Supabase's `postgres` is not a superuser and "cannot `set role app_user`", a role it made itself (`STATUS.md` line 400). _Proof:_ here, as the tables' owner made like Supabase's (not a superuser, may create roles; its memberships show `admin_option t, set_option f`): `ERROR: must be able to SET ROLE "queue_owner"`. What did work, as the same owner: `grant queue_owner to <the owner> with set true, inherit false;` then the `create schema`, then `revoke all on schema pgboss from public` (as `queue_owner`), then `revoke queue_owner from <the owner>`. With that schema, the worker's own login holding `queue_owner` started at once (case W6). Without it the worker refuses in plain words (case W5: "the pgboss schema does not exist (the release makes it, record 053)"). _Why it matters beyond Test 2:_ step 2.112's done test runs "on PGlite", where everything runs as a superuser, so it would pass and the migration would still fail on the test copy and in production, stopping the release there. Every invitation email, import and nightly purge waits for the worker. _Spec:_ T-257, record 053, T7 §1. Proposed step P5.

**H4. When something breaks, nobody is told.** No error report leaves either program: `packages/observability` has a Sentry adapter, but no file in `apps/web` or `apps/worker` imports the error reporter (`grep`), and there is no setting for it. No outside check exists (T8 §7: every minute, the home page, one league page, the website's health and the worker's heartbeat). No alert goes to a phone (T-159: site down, errors spiking, a job waiting over 10 minutes, the database nearly full, bounces rising). No dashboard (T-151), no status page, no game-night watch (T-160). Step 2.95 writes three procedures; nothing in any plan builds the rest (the 2.105 audit's finding M15 left them to this one). Two facts make it harder: the worker's health answer does not yet carry the waiting jobs or the age of the oldest (`apps/worker/src/start-worker.ts`, header: "Not here yet"), and a worker run as Render's "background worker" type takes no requests from outside as Render describes the type (to confirm on the account), so its health address cannot be checked from outside at all: the web's health answer must carry the queue's last look instead. _Proof:_ `grep -n -i "uptime\|dashboard\|Sentry\|status page" docs/build/STAGE-2.md` finds only this step's own line. _Spec:_ T8 §7, T-142, T-151, T-159, T-160; T10 stage 1 ("error reporting; uptime checks"). Not needed for the supervised session, where the founder and the lead are watching; needed before anyone else relies on the copy. Proposed step P6.

**H5. No backup has ever been restored, no procedure says how, and no step will try one.** Continuous backup is off (STAGE-1-REPORT, "Continuous backup … Off"). On Supabase's free plan, as Supabase describes it, there are no backups a project can restore from (to confirm); T8 §4 promises at most 5 minutes of data lost and 4 hours to be running again, "practised, not assumed". T-154's quarterly rehearsal, T-153's continuous backup and T-155's one-league restore are in no step; step 2.95's line names "restoring the database" among its procedures, to be "written once followed in the supervised session", but nothing in the session restores anything. _What was tried here:_ a dump of a database holding two made-up leagues, made as the tables' owner, restored into an empty database on the same server, brought back every row and rule (6.6). _What it showed a real restore must add:_ the dump carries 84 grants to `app_user` and `sign_in_store` and no role at all, so onto a new server the roles and logins come first (with new passwords) or the fence's grants fail; and the people's sign-ins live in Supabase's own schema, which a dump of ours does not carry. _Spec:_ T8 §4 and §5, T-153, T-154, T-155; LEADS.md row 7 ("backups that have been restored once"). Proposed step P7.

### Medium

**M1. One sentence for every database problem at start.** A wrong password (case 15), a certificate from an unknown authority (case 11) and a database that is not there (case 16) all print "The web app cannot start: the database could not be reached to check its login role."; the worker the same (case W4). The league-making tool names the likely cause (`scripts/make-league.messages.mjs`: "the user name or password, the database name, the host, the network, a time limit, or the certificate file"). On Render's log, in the session, the lead cannot tell a certificate from a password. The driver's own message is rightly not repeated (it may hold the address); the kind can be told from its code without it. Part of P1.

**M2. Staging and production accept a plain-http public address, and one with a path.** `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` is checked only for http or https (`config-schema.ts:43-49`). _Proof:_ case 20, production with `http://test-copy.example.test/sub`, passed every setting check and stopped only at "not wired yet". Session cookies are marked Secure only "when the site is on HTTPS" (`apps/web/src/server/sign-in/cookies.ts:2`), so one wrong letter sends them unprotected. The worker already refuses a path. _Spec:_ T4 §5. Proposed step P9.

**M3. Whether `TRUSTED_PROXY=one` is right on Render is unknown.** Staging and production must set it (case 2), and `one` believes the last address added by "exactly one proxy of the host" (`config-schema.ts`). How many proxies stand in front of a Render service is not known from here. If it is not one, every visitor shares one address and one person's wrong passwords lock out everyone, or a visitor can choose the address they are counted under. `none` is accepted in production (case 21). Step 2.98 holds the choice for Cloudflare. _In the session:_ wrong passwords on one phone must not lock out a second phone on another network (section 10, step 18).

**M4 (TEST 2). Nothing on the test copy says it is made up, and it takes anyone's address.** The line "A made-up league on this computer. It starts over when the app restarts." is drawn by the stand-in only (`packages/site/src/messages/en/site.ts:38-39`, "never on a real league"). On the test copy, a league made with the league-making tool looks like a real one to anyone who opens its Render address, and nothing reminds a tester not to type real people's names. And because "Allow new sign-ups" is on at Supabase (record 018), a stranger who finds the address can sign up with their own, real, email address: real people's data on a copy that must hold made-up data only (T-13, T-201). _Spec:_ T-13, T-201, CLAUDE.md ("made-up data only"). Proposed step P3: a notice on every page of the test copy, and sign-up refused there for any address that is not a made-up one (the same list record 075 keeps for kept emails).

**M5. The supervised session's checks on real PostgreSQL are about forty, written as prose, with no tool.** Four reviews wrote them onto step 2.93's line (part 3, step 2.187, part 4, part 6). The two-league harness that runs the same kind of check on every change takes the in-process database only (`packages/database/src/isolation/two-leagues.test-helper.ts:678-684`: `openTwoLeagues` makes a PGlite). The STAGE-1 report asked for "the two-league test against" the test copy; no tool can run it there. Proposed step P18.

**M6. Of the eight written procedures T8 §11 asks for, none exists.** `docs/operations/` has guides for running locally, applying migrations, making and removing a league, and the tracker's hosting, but not one of T8's list: releasing and reversing, restoring the database, rotating a secret (all three planned in step 2.95), suspending and restoring a league, a bounce or complaint spike, granting support access, responding to an incident (T-84: "before the first outside league joins"), and the game-night checklist (step 2.82 writes a rehearsal checklist). T-165: "a procedure counts as written only after someone has followed it start to finish." The 2.105 audit's M15 left these to this audit. Proposed step P8.

**M7. A Render key in an AI session's reach would reach production too.** "Needs the founder" asks for "its API key on the `RENDER_API_KEY` line" of `.env.staging` (`STATUS.md` line 54). A Render API key acts for its owner across every service the owner can reach, settings included, and the services' settings will hold the database logins and the sign-in service's secret key. Today only the test copy exists; the day production lives in the same Render account, the key in `.env.staging` reaches production's secrets, against T-201 ("never holds production secrets"). Also, `make-a-league.md` says the database addresses "never pass through an AI session", while CLAUDE.md lets the lead use `.env.staging` in a session the founder started: the two should say the same. _Spec:_ T-201, T-166. Corrected in the founder's checklist (section 9) and part of P4.

**M8. The online scoring pilot carries 32 known holes, two of them critical in what it runs, and its record read only seven.** `apps/varsity-hosted` (its own lockfile; the root `npm audit` cannot see it). _Proof:_ `npm audit --package-lock-only` there: 2 critical, 13 high, 16 moderate, 1 low. Its `next` 16.3.4 is named in twelve advisories, three of them critical (remote code execution in `next/og`'s ImageResponse, GHSA-vcvr-r3jv-pc5j; unauthenticated remote code execution in the image optimizer with SVG, GHSA-2464-fhr4-w9xw; unauthenticated remote code execution in `'use cache'` functions returning typed arrays, GHSA-673q-mjm6-r5xr). Record 079 weighed seven, those of Next's November release, and found the pilot clear of each because vinext replaces Next's server. But `react-server-dom-webpack` 19.2.6, a direct dependency of the pilot that its server build is made with (`@vitejs/plugin-rsc` 0.5.26, its React Server Components plugin), so in what it runs as far as reading the build can tell, is named in "React: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution in React Server Components" (GHSA-xqc2-xf4c-x3h3, critical, fixed in 19.2.9) and a denial of service in server functions (GHSA-wx67-qw84-cm4g, high). What stands between a stranger and that code is the host: the pilot is "owner-private. Sites performs sign-in/access enforcement before invoking this app" (`apps/varsity-hosted/README.md`). The founder's line in `STATUS.md` says "nothing is at risk as far as its code can tell"; that is no longer what the advisories say. It is not the platform, so it does not stop Test 2. _Spec:_ T-283, T9 §9, T-15 (the pilot is retired after Al-Hadi's move). Proposed step P11.

**M9. Nothing tells anyone when a pinned release gains a hole.** Step 2.99 (the dependency scan in `ci.yml`, weekly update proposals, both lockfiles) is parked and on no test line; record 079 says so ("Until step 2.99 is built nothing tells the team"). The root lockfile today names three, all in test tools never shipped (vitest 3.2.7 critical through tinypool, @vitest/mocker moderate); the only offered fix is a major release, so it is the lead's call, as step 2.99's line says. No step adopts framework majors "within about six months" (T9 §9). Proposed step P12.

**M10. Every signed-in request asks the sign-in service, and a restart during its outage takes the whole site down.** `liveSession` (`packages/providers/src/sign-in/supabase/supabase-sign-in.ts:205`) calls Supabase's `/user` for each signed-in request, to catch a session ended there. While Supabase's sign-in service is down or slow, every signed-in page and every tap a scorekeeper sends fails (a timeout or a 5xx is thrown, not taken as signed out: `gotrue-client.ts`, `call`). Visitors are not affected, until the website restarts: then step 2.115's check cannot get its answer and the website refuses to start at all (case 19: "the sign-in service could not say whether it confirms email addresses (it could not be reached)"), so a deploy or a host restart during a sign-in outage takes the public pages down too. T8 §12 has no row for the sign-in service. How long the extra call takes on Render is unmeasured. _Spec:_ T8 §12, T-151. Part of P20: a row in T8 §12, a decision (for example: start-up keeps the last answer it got, or a restart in staging and production waits and asks again rather than ending), and the time measured in the session.

**M11. How the database logins are made is written nowhere.** The website's login `app_login` was "made outside migrations" by the lead on 2026-11-13 (`STATUS.md` line 400); no procedure says how (`create role … login password …; grant app_user to …;`), who keeps its password, or how it is changed. Step 2.112 makes the website refuse a login that is a member of `queue_owner`, so the worker needs a login of its own, made the same way and granted `queue_owner`; that too is written nowhere. Made here exactly so (6.2). _Spec:_ T-60, T8 §11 ("rotating a secret"). Part of P4.

**M12. The outside services' limits and costs: unwritten, and none is watched.** As each vendor describes its free plan (to be confirmed at sign-up, T-167): a Supabase free project is paused after about a week without activity, and the repository's keep-awake workflow wakes only the tracker's project (`.github/workflows/keep-supabase-awake.yml` reads `vars.SUPABASE_URL`, the tracker's); a free database is limited to 500 MB and is then made read-only, which is the "full disk" of this area, and nobody would be told; a Render free instance sleeps after 15 minutes and takes about a minute to wake (T-270), so the first phone at tip-off waits. Spending alerts on every account (T8 §10) are in no plan. Corrected in the founder's checklist; part of P6.

**M13. The tracker's own database connection does not check who it talks to, and its address can switch encryption off.** The 2.125 review's question. `connectPostgres` (`packages/database/src/live-stats/postgres.ts:335-347`) removes five encryption keys from the address but not `ssl` or `sslnegotiation`, and without `DATABASE_CA` it encrypts without checking the server (`rejectUnauthorized: false`). _Proof_, each in its own process against the local server: no CA, encrypted but unchecked; `?ssl=0` with the CA given: `encrypted: false`; `?ssl=no-verify` with the CA given: encrypted, check off; `?ssl=false`: the process ends with `TypeError: Cannot use 'in' operator to search for 'key' in false` inside `pg`. It matters because this is what `npm run stats:db-check`, `npm run stats:copy` and the tracker's server mode use with `DATABASE_URL`, on the founder's laptop, against the live tracker's database, which holds real children's names; on a shared network, an unchecked connection can be listened to. The live site itself does not use it (it talks to Supabase from the browser). Who fixes it: a small step in `packages/database/src/live-stats` with the tracker's tests, not around a game; the founder can close most of it today by putting the certificate in `DATABASE_CA` (`.env.example` line 108). Proposed step P10.

**M14. No size or speed figure has ever been measured** (2.105 audit, its lines 634, 800 and 856). T8 §1's sizes are "design targets … claims only after they are measured"; T6 §10's targets (a tap visible to viewers within 2 seconds, 95 times in 100); T8 §8's budgets (main content in 2.5 seconds on a mid-range phone; 300 and 800 ms answers; admin under 1 second); T-161's automatic check of the budgets. Only the size budget is planned (2.99). In Test 2 a watcher's page asks again about every 7 seconds (2.93's line), so T6's 2 seconds will not be met and the founder should be told so beforehand. Proposed step P13.

**M15. No check finds a list that is not paged** (2.105 audit, its line 841: T8 line 29, "every list is paged and every input is capped"). People are paged; step 2.90 found one list that is not; nothing asks every list. One more, for this audit to weigh (step 2.93 part 6): `listGameNames` (`packages/database/src/queries/list-game-names.ts`) reads every team, every season and every scorekeeper assignment of the league each time the games area names its games. For a league of size A (30 games a season) that is a few hundred rows after a decade and harmless; for an association (6,000 games a season) it grows by thousands of rows a season, and is read by every scheduler and scorekeeper opening the games area. A season filter (the games shown, or the seasons they belong to) is needed before the first association's second season, not before Test 2. Proposed step P14.

**M16. How long logs are kept is decided nowhere** (2.105 audit, its line 756: T-86, "logs kept 90 days"). The website and the worker write structured lines to their output; how long Render keeps them depends on the plan (to confirm), and nothing sends them anywhere else. The first incident's question ("what happened to this game?", T-196) needs them. Proposed step P15.

**M17. There is no preview copy of a proposed change** (2.105 audit, M14: T8 line 78, T1 §6, T-180, which makes trying the preview the founder's way of reviewing anything). Nothing plans one. Render's own previews are, as Render describes them, a paid team feature (to confirm); the cheapest honest answer is a preview run on the made-up stand-in, which needs no database. Not for Test 2. Proposed step P16.

**M18. No browser test runs against the test copy after a release** (2.105 audit, M14: T8 line 79). Step 2.95 does not have it. In the session the walk does it by hand; after that, every release should be followed by a short, read-only run against the test copy. Proposed step P17.

**M19. Neither program checks that the database is at the changes its code expects.** Neither `startup.ts` nor `start-worker.ts` reads the migration log (`grep migration_log apps/web/src apps/worker/src`: nothing). An older image on a newer database is the designed case (T-49, enforced by the drop-and-rename check, and the runner accepts a database ahead: 6.2); but a newer image started before its changes are applied (a restart by the host, a deploy started by hand) runs against a schema it does not know and fails on the first request that needs the new table, as an error page. Step 2.95's "a failing migration starts nothing" covers only its own release command. Part of P4.

**M20 (TEST 2). Four things step 2.95's line does not settle.** (1) **Deploying on every push.** If the Render service follows the build branch, every landing restarts the test copy, during the founder's walk too; the release command's T-158 check (no release while games are live) is skipped by any deploy that does not go through it. The test copy should be deployed only by hand, from a named commit. (2) **Where the database changes run.** A release command that applies migrations "and only then starts the new version" needs a place to run before the new version starts; Render's "pre-deploy command" is, as Render describes it, for paid instances only (to confirm), and the test copy's website is on the free one. (3) **The tracker's project file.** The website and the worker refuse to start in staging and production when `supabase/site.json` cannot be found above their code ("supabase/site.json: could not be read, so … cannot be checked against the tracker's project", `platform-database-guard.ts:206`); an image that installs "only what it needs" (R10) could leave it out. (4) **Going back.** What "the previous version" is on Render (an image tag, a commit), and that going back has been done once on the test copy with a game in its history and the table unchanged. Proposed step P4.

### Low

**L1. Some refusals do not say what is allowed.** "TRUSTED_PROXY: invalid, not one of the allowed values", "LOG_LEVEL: invalid, not one of the allowed values", "PUBLIC_BASE_URL: invalid, wrong format" (case 4), "APP_ENV: invalid, not one of the allowed values" (case 5). Naming the allowed words (`none` or `one`; `local`, `test`, `staging`, `production`) prints no secret. Part of P9.

**L2. Next.js prints "✓ Ready" before the website refuses to start** (every case in 6.1). Someone reading Render's log line by line may think it started. Harmless; worth one sentence in the release procedure.

**L3. While the database is away, the worker writes about three lines a second, none of them plain.** About 240 lines in 80 seconds, each `{"level":"error","msg":"worker.queue_error","kind":"error","errorCode":"unexpected"}`, and no line when the database comes back. The health address says it well (6.5); the log buries everything else on a plan that keeps few lines. One line when the queue loses its database and one when it has it again would do.

**L4. pg-boss's tables end up owned by the worker's login, not by `queue_owner`.** Here, 13 tables in `pgboss`, owner `worker_login`. Record 053 means the schema to be `queue_owner`'s; a second worker login (a change of logins, not of password) could not upgrade them. Step 2.112 (P5) can decide whether the worker sets its role to `queue_owner` first.

**L5. T8 §12, the table of failures, has no row for four of this area's** (the sign-in service down, a full disk, a leaked key, a wrong deletion). Section 6.7 has what each does today. Part of P19.

**L6. `apply-migrations.md` is out of date.** "Today there are eleven" (there are twenty) and "It has not yet been run against a hosted database" (it was, on 2026-11-13); the second is already on step 2.95's line. Part of P19.

**L7. `make-a-league.md` lists step 2.115 as still missing** before a real school's league (line 148); it landed on 2026-11-16. Part of P19.

**L8. The worker's capture outside production keeps every address and never removes a file** (record 075, "Not done yet"). On the host's disk that is a slow leak of whatever addresses the worker was given. Part of P2.

**L9. The web's health answer does not ask the database** (`apps/web/src/server/health.ts`: "It does not ping the database on each call"). Planned in 2.93's last part; listed so that the outside check of P6 is pointed at an answer that means "the site can read its data", not only "the program started".

## 6. Each part as it stands

### 6.1 Start-up: what each program refuses to start without

The built website was started with `node scripts/web.mjs start`, and the worker with `node apps/worker/src/main.ts`, each with nothing in its environment but the settings named (`env -i`), all of them made up. "Local database" means the PostgreSQL 16 server of section 2, its certificate signed by a made-up authority; "the stand-in" is a program on this computer answering the sign-in service's one start-up question. Every run ended with exit code 1 unless it says otherwise, and every website run printed Next.js's "✓ Ready" first (L2). No run printed a value, an address or a key.

### 6.2 The database

All run with the repository's own runner against the local PostgreSQL 16, as a tables' owner made like Supabase's (`createrole`, `bypassrls`, not a superuser).

- **An empty database:** all 20 files applied in 413 ms, certificate checked against the made-up authority. Run again: nothing applied, 85 ms. Without the authority's file: "CONNECT FAILED: unable to verify the first certificate" (the same wall as H1).
- **Where the test copy stands:** files 0001 to 0009 applied to a new database (293 ms), then today's folder: 0010 to 0020 applied (236 ms), no error.
- **A copy that already holds leagues:** an older tree of the code (the commit before migration 0020) loaded the two made-up seed leagues into an in-process database; today's runner then applied 0020 on top. Of 47 tables, only the migration log changed (19 to 20 rows) and the two new tables appeared empty; neither league got a site row, which is what the 2.187 review expects ("they show the neutral design"). The seed cannot be loaded onto a real PostgreSQL (it takes a PGlite by design), so this was the in-process database, real PostgreSQL inside the program.
- **A change that fails half-way:** a made-up file 0021 that makes a table, puts a row in it and then divides by zero. Answer: `"code":"migration_failed","file":"0021_made_up_failure.sql","message":"0021_made_up_failure.sql failed and was rolled back: division by zero"`. Afterwards the log still ends at 20 and the table does not exist. In a release of several files, the ones before the failure stay applied (each file is its own transaction), which is safe only because every file must leave the previous version working (T-49).
- **Taking a change back:** there are no "down" files, by design (T-156: going back means running the previous version against the newer database). The runner, given the older folder (0001 to 0019) against the newer database, answered `"ok":true`, `"newerInDatabase":["0020_league_sites.sql"]` and changed nothing. What makes this safe is the drop-and-rename check on every change (`npm run check`: "T-183 no drop or rename in one migration step", passed). Neither program checks at start which changes the database holds (M19).
- **The roles the procedures name.** `app_user` (made by 0005) and `sign_in_store` (0012) are made by the files; neither can log in. The website's login is made by hand, as on the test copy on 2026-11-13: `create role app_login login password '…'; grant app_user to app_login;` then `grant sign_in_store to app_login;` (make-a-league.md step 2), which the tables' owner may run because it made `sign_in_store`. Its memberships show why it may not go further: `admin_option t, inherit_option f, set_option f` for every role it made. Signed in as `app_login`, after `set local role app_user`: not a superuser, not bypassing the fence, 0 leagues and 0 rows of `profile_access` with no league set, and `create table` refused ("permission denied for schema public"). `app_login` cannot use the `pgboss` schema. The queue's schema (step 2.112) failed as written (H3) and was made with the temporary self-grant; the worker's own login, `create role worker_login login …; grant app_user, queue_owner to worker_login;`, then started the worker (W6).

What checks there are, and what they do not cover:

- **Browser code:** `npm run check` passed here: "T-30 no settings or secrets in browser code" scans the source for reads of settings and for the shapes of keys. It does not read what the build produces. A build made here with five made-up secrets in its settings (a database password inside its address, the sign-in service's key, a Resend key, a Stripe key and the session secret) left none of them anywhere in `apps/web/.next`, the browser's files or the server's, nor in the build's own output. The website reads no `NEXT_PUBLIC_` setting, the only kind Next.js copies into browser code. Step 2.99 puts that scan of the built files into the gate.
- **Logs and start-up messages:** none of the 28 cases printed a value; the logger hides any field whose name contains "email" (`start-worker.ts`: "the logger hides any key with that word in it (T-86)"). The kept emails' codes never reach a log (record 075, tested).
- **Error pages:** not checked. The website cannot serve in staging or production yet, and Next.js's own production error page is what a visitor would see.
- **The repository:** a search of every commit in the history for the shapes of Supabase secret keys, signed tokens, Resend and Stripe keys and database addresses with a password found only made-up values (`sb_secret_made_up_0123`, `sb_secret_fake…`, `re_abcdefghijk…`, `sk_live_abcdef…`, and pooler addresses whose user is a template such as `postgres.${ref}` or `postgres.abcdefghijklmnopqrst`). It is not in the gate: step 2.99's committed-secret scan, and GitHub's own secret scanning (the founder's checklist, item 9).
- **The image:** does not exist yet. Step 2.95 must make sure no `.env` file is copied into it.

### 6.4 Releases

- **How a release is made:** it is not. There is no image of the website or the worker (`Dockerfile` is the tracker's), no release command, no workflow that builds or publishes an image (`ci.yml` runs the gate and the browser tests, and builds the scoring pilot), no description of the Render services. All of it is step 2.95.
- **How one is taken back:** not built, and never run, even on a computer: there is nothing to run. What exists is what makes it possible later: database changes that leave the previous version working (T-49, checked on every change) and a runner that accepts a database ahead of its folder (6.2).
- **What a person watching a live game sees during a release** (read, not run): the watcher's page keeps the last score on the screen and asks again at its next turn when a request fails (`apps/web/src/features/live-game/follow-game.ts`: a failed fetch is caught; the page asks every 5 seconds while it has no live connection, and on the test copy it asks about every 7 seconds anyway); the scorekeeper's taps are written to the device first and sent in order until answered (live-scoring audit, step 2.12); a scorekeeper who reloads while the website is away sees "Opening the game…" until it answers (live-scoring audit, line 258). On Render's free instance the website also sleeps after 15 minutes with no visitor and takes about a minute to wake (T-270).
- **No release while games are live (T-158):** on step 2.95's line, for its release command only (M20).

### 6.5 The worker and its queue

- **It starts** (W6), on PostgreSQL 16, in staging mode, with pg-boss, once its schema exists; pg-boss then made its 13 tables there itself, owned by the worker's login (L4).
- **When the database goes away** (stopped for 80 seconds under a running worker, then started again): the process kept running; its health address (`/health` on `WORKER_HEALTH_PORT`) answered `{"status":"ok",…,"secondsSinceBeat":51}` with 200 for the first minute, then `{"status":"down","app":"worker","queue":"pg-boss","secondsSinceBeat":61}` with 503, and `{"status":"ok",…,"secondsSinceBeat":0}` again within 5 seconds of the database's return, with nothing done by hand. Its log meanwhile: L3.
- **Can a job run twice?** Yes, by design: "jobs may run more than once; their effects may not" (T-137). A job is handed to pg-boss under its own id, so a worker that crashes between handing it over and marking it hands it over again and pg-boss keeps one (`pg-boss-queue.ts`, header). Each job's own safety on a second run is tested beside it (the 2.105 audit's row T7-17); not re-run here.
- **Can a job be lost?** Not while the worker is down: a job is saved in the same transaction as the change that caused it (T-7), and waits. After its last attempt, a failing job goes to pg-boss's failed list, where nobody is told (T-142, H4) and nothing can run it again (the 2.105 audit's row T7-17).
- **On the test copy:** it cannot start until the queue's schema exists (H3), so no invitation email, import or nightly purge would happen there; none is needed for the walk. A worker on Render's "background worker" type cannot be checked from outside (H4).

### 6.6 Backups and restore

- **Written:** nothing. Step 2.95's line names a procedure for "restoring the database"; no file exists.
- **Tried on Supabase:** never. Continuous backup is off; what the free plan keeps, and whether it can be restored, is as Supabase describes its plans (to confirm in the session).
- **Tried here:** the two made-up leagues were copied into a database on the local PostgreSQL, which was dumped with `pg_dump -Fc` as the tables' owner (362 KB, 0.13 s) and restored with `pg_restore` into an empty database on the same server. Every count matched: 47 fence rules, 48 tables with the fence forced, 119 grants to `app_user`, 29 to `sign_in_store`, 20 migrations logged, 2 leagues, 8 accounts, 5 people. On the restored copy, `app_login` with no league set saw 0 leagues. The dump holds 84 `GRANT` lines naming `app_user` and `sign_in_store` and no `CREATE ROLE` at all.
- **What a restore would lose, as things stand:** with no continuous backup, everything since the last backup the plan keeps, which T8 §4 says may be at most 5 minutes; onto a new server, the roles and logins unless made first (and the logins' passwords, which are not in any backup of ours); with a dump of our schemas alone, every person's sign-in, since Supabase keeps those in its own schema; the jobs waiting in pg-boss's schema, unless it is included; and on the host, the worker's captured emails. Uploaded files do not exist yet.

### 6.8 What a stranger can reach on the test copy

- **The local sign-in pages** (`/signin/kept-emails`, `/signin/made-up-people` and the "be this person" action): refused by construction, three times over (record 075): the app's own `APP_ENV` must be local or test; the request must come from this computer and not through another server; only ports made on made-up data carry the tools. Proved on the server's own functions (`apps/web/src/server/local-only.test.ts`, passed here), not yet over the network: that byte-for-byte comparison is on 2.93's line for when staging can serve. The made-up world cannot be started there at all (case 10, and the stand-in refuses any public address that is not local or `.test`).
- **Unfinished pages:** the test copy is not production, so step 2.140 is not on the Test 2 line; an admin area not built yet says "This part of the admin is not ready yet." (step 2.171). Acceptable for a test copy.
- **"Do not index":** not built (`grep -ri "x-robots\|robots" apps/web`: nothing). Planned in 2.93's last part, on every response outside production and in `robots.txt`.
- **Made-up data plainly made up:** not on the test copy (M4).
- **Signing up:** open to anyone with any address (M4).

### 6.9 Dependencies

- **The website and the worker** (the root lockfile): `npm audit` names three, all in test tools that are never shipped: `vitest` 3.2.7 (critical, through `tinypool`'s prototype-pollution advisories) and `@vitest/mocker` (moderate); the only fix offered is `vitest` 5.1.0, a major release. Nothing in `next` (16.4.6, record 079). The command's own advice to run `npm audit fix --force` was not followed, by rule.
- **The scoring pilot** (`apps/varsity-hosted`, its own lockfile): 32, of which 2 critical, 13 high, 16 moderate and 1 low. Besides `next` and `react-server-dom-webpack` (M8): `vinext` (through `@vercel/og` and `image-size`), `wrangler`, `miniflare`, `vite`, `@cloudflare/vite-plugin`, `sharp`, `undici`, `ws`, `esbuild`, `drizzle-kit`, `js-yaml`, `browserslist` and others, most of them build tools.
- **Keeping pins current:** by hand, when someone notices (record 079, T-283). Step 2.99 is the plan, and it is parked (M9).

And the supervised session itself, as the STAGE-1 report described it ("connect the test copy … start the website and the worker on Render behind Cloudflare, send yourself an invitation and accept it, switch on continuous backup, ship a release and then take it back, and set the uptime checks"), is replaced by section 10: no Cloudflare, no worker and no invitation in the first session (none is on the Test 2 line), no backup for made-up data, and the uptime check only once step P6 has given it something to point at.

## 10. THE SUPERVISED SESSION, IN ORDER

For the founder and the lead together, in a session the founder starts. The founder types every address, password and key; the lead reads the screen with them and never holds them. If what is seen at a step is not what this list says, stop there and do not go on.

**Before the day**

1. _Lead:_ every step on the Test 2 line has landed, and so have P1 to P4. GitHub has passed the commit to be released twice. Its id is written in `STATUS.md`. _See:_ the id, and "PASSED" twice for it.
2. _Lead:_ the walk of Test 1 done once on this computer on that commit. _See:_ the final table right, as worked in the numbers audit.
3. _Founder:_ checklist items 1, 3 and 4 done. _See:_ the new database lines in `.env.staging` (the founder, not the lead), the certificate file in the folder, a Render account with two-step sign-in.

**Setting up the test database**

4. _Founder reads aloud:_ the test project's reference in the Supabase dashboard, and the one in `supabase/site.json`. _See:_ they are different.
5. _Founder:_ in the dashboard, Authentication, Sign In / Providers, Email: "Confirm email" on. _See:_ the switch on.
6. _Founder, at their terminal:_ apply the database changes with step 2.95's release command, as the tables' owner, the certificate checked. _See:_ the changes after 0009 listed as applied, up to the newest; run again, nothing applied.
7. _Founder, in the SQL editor:_ `grant sign_in_store to app_login;` _See:_ "Success" (or that it is already granted).
8. _Lead and founder:_ the checks on real PostgreSQL from step 2.93's line (P18's script, or by hand). _See:_ every one as its line says; any other answer stops the session.

**Starting the website**

9. _Founder, in Render:_ a web service from the image of the commit of step 1, on the free instance, with automatic deploys off. Its settings, typed by the founder: `APP_ENV=staging`; `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` = the service's own `https://….onrender.com` address; `EMAIL_FROM` = a made-up sender; `TRUSTED_PROXY=one` (proved at step 18); `PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL` = `app_login`'s address; the certificate (P1's setting); `SUPABASE_URL`; `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`; `LOG_LEVEL=info`. Nothing else: no `DATABASE_URL`, no `RESEND_API_KEY`, no Stripe key, nothing starting `LOCAL_`. _See:_ the list matches, one by one.
10. _Deploy, and read the log together._ _See:_ no line beginning "The app cannot start" or "The web app cannot start"; the health address (`/api/v1/health`) answers 200 with `"status":"ok"` and its database check.
11. _From a phone, signed out:_ any page of the copy. _See:_ the test-copy notice (P3); the page's headers say `noindex` and `/robots.txt` says the same.
12. _From a phone:_ `/signin/kept-emails`, `/signin/made-up-people` and `/signin/no-such-page`. _See:_ the same "not found" page for all three (the lead compares the answers byte for byte, as 2.93's line says).
13. _From a phone:_ sign up with a real-looking address that is not made up. _See:_ refused in plain words (P3).

**The league and its owner**

14. _Founder, at their terminal:_ `npm run league:make -- --hosted` for a practice league, following [make-a-league.md](../../operations/make-a-league.md) steps 4 and 5. _See:_ the "Where" line names the test project and says "NOT on this computer"; it is made.
15. _Founder:_ `npm run league:remove -- --hosted` for that practice league. _See:_ removed, its short name free again, one line in the platform's log.
16. _Founder:_ the real made-up league (make-a-league.md steps 6 to 12), with a made-up owner address (ending `.test`) and "who plays" said aloud. _See:_ one league in draft, one season, two activity lines, an owner's account not yet signed in.
17. _On a phone:_ sign up as the owner with that address; at the terminal, the founder reads the code with P2's script and types it on the phone; choose a password. _See:_ signed in, and the league's admin opens.
18. _On phone A:_ sign in with a wrong password until refused; _on phone B, on mobile data:_ sign in with the right one. _See:_ phone B is let in. If it is refused, stop: `TRUSTED_PROXY` is wrong for Render (M3).

**The walk**

19. _On the phones:_ step 2.194's written walk: teams and their people, rounds and games, the schedule published, the season shown, one game scored live on phone A from tip-off to "final" while phone B watches signed out. _See:_ phone B follows within about 7 seconds (not 2: M14); the game ends; the final table is right.
20. _With a game live:_ try a release with the release command. _See:_ refused until told to go ahead (T-158).
21. _After the game:_ release the next commit, then take it back to the first. _See:_ the version the health address names changes and comes back; the game, its box score and the table are unchanged; the log shows no database change undone.
22. _On two phones:_ the checks of 2.93's line that need a browser (names hidden in a private window; no surname, email or birth date in the page's source; the pages answer `private, no-store`). _See:_ each as written.

**Before leaving**

23. _Founder:_ decide whether the copy stays up (free) or the service is suspended; delete any Render API key made for the session. _Lead:_ write into the stage report what was proved, what failed and what was not tried, and mark each procedure followed today "followed on (date)" (T-165).
